## Reasoning effort

A reason
ing effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**, not a free-standing\nfield. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `source`, an op
tional `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallback`) carries it as `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is\naccepted everywhere a

model choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.modelSele
ction` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure-adho
c`) | `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |\n| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`, read back
on the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`, read back on
ls.** `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of\n them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEfforts`
on each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n that model; do no
t guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded on the

execution record, or refused with
 `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling
 temperature.
* **
A selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins
its own model. A bare model\n change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model\n instead of failing.\
n* **Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's e
xisting selection for that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a clie
nt `set`, an environment\n or a suite, keeping the bare model id.\n* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an

unknown key
 (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.
* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`
 reports `
modelSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied,

so
 writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored
 value is refused by the runner.

`POST /
chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a\nper-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the ses
sion's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved selection carries

, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.

The SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operations:
`
--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits the selection the target\nalready has, and is refused (`send modelSelectio

n`) when there is none.

## Not in the API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** available over the API

today (most exist in the hosted inspector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design; see [Authentication](#auth

entication))
* Chat and conformance suites
* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth yourself,
 then up

load the token to one of the server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Discord](https://d

iscord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z); it directly shapes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned*
* (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **During the preview*
*, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).\
n* **Additive changes** (new endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes) are considered non-b
reaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.\n* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error **

messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is
**stu
dy**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the\noperation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing resp

onse fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/stu
dies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/…`
|\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/projects/{pr
ojectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` | `/
projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-overvi
ew`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/ins

ights` |

Response fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, and

`sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`get_user_testing_s
cenario` served the environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are\n
absent rather than null when you may not have them.\n\n**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including its old response
\nspellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. The old paths are not in the Ope

nAPI spec, and they are removed
at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the rename and so ha
ve no\ndeprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and ac

cept either, never both in
one request, until general availability.

### Vocabulary

Renamed field values cannot be aliased t

he way paths are, so they are chosen
by header. Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read
canonically:

|

Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `parentRef.kind`
| `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `stu

dyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |
| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, w
hich is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a
path segment\nby either spelling; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one. A response that varies by vocabulary sends\n

`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is
eval-scoped by name a
nd moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so read\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` (`a
piVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are\ntwo blocks) before sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2

})`, or
`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink resource types work differently: `study` and
`goal_
run` are the canonical keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response
carries follows the\nOPERATION rather than the header; a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the ol

d one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.
